title: Read Linux Permission Strings
summary: Decode -rwxr-x--- and drwxr-x---: file kind and permission triplets.

sketchBlocks.title: Read Linux Permission Strings
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A Linux permission listing is a concise summary of the file type, access bits, ownership, and other metadata. Before changing a permission, read the existing permissions and understand the intended users.

```bash
pwd
ls -l
ls -l secure-lab
```

An *illustrative* `ls -l` line looks like this:

```text
-rwxr-x--- 1 learner study 82 Nov 9 10:20 run.sh
```

The first character (`-`) means a regular file; a leading `d` means directory; `l` indicates a symbolic link. The next nine characters are three groups: `rwx | r-x | ---`, describing owner, group, and everyone else respectively. `r` allows reading, `w` allows writing, `x` allows executing an eligible file. The dash indicates a missing bit. This is not a guarantee that an operation will succeed: the active identity, all parent directories, and other filesystem controls can affect effective access.

| Mode field | Type | Owner | Group | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-rw-r-----` | file | `rw-` | `r--` | `---` |
| `drwxr-x---` | directory | `rwx` | `r-x` | `---` |
| `-rwx------` | file | `rwx` | `---` | `---` |

**Worked example:** For `-rw-r-----`, the owning user can read and modify the file. Members of the owning group may read it (assuming parent traversal). Everyone else has none of those permission bits. Nobody has the execute bit. Do not confuse the leading file-type dash with the owner execute bit.

quizDraft.title: Audit three named entries
quizDraft.prompt:
**Try it yourself**

A teammate needs a compact read-only inventory of the practice workspace.

1. Run `ls -ld secure-lab`.
2. Run `ls -l secure-lab/README.md secure-lab/private-note.txt`.
3. Run `ls -ld secure-lab/shared`.
4. Interpret the first ten mode characters on every line.

**Check your work:** You can distinguish the type character and all three triplets for two files and two directories without modifying anything.

*Use only the supplied practice files; avoid sudo, recursive chmod, and system changes.*
quizDraft.hint: For each result, read type, owner `rwx`, group `rwx`, then other `rwx` in that order.

help.concept: You can distinguish the type character and all three triplets for two files and two directories without modifying anything.
help.hint_2: For each result, read type, owner `rwx`, group `rwx`, then other `rwx` in that order.
